title: A kinder way to end the group-chat spiral
audio: Silent; no music or recorded voiceover.
captionSidecarNote: SRT covers the full duration with draft voiceover text; the video itself is silent.
caption: The group chat doesn’t need another “I’m good with anything.” Offer two options, add a time and one useful detail, then leave room for a real answer. A simple plan is still a plan.
cta: Save this for the next time the chat gets stuck.

scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: The group chat wants to hang out. Nobody can pick a plan.
Try two options instead of an open-ended question.

scenes.onScreen: 10 AM · easy pace · meet at the entrance
scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: Add a time and the detail everyone needs.
Then let people answer without pressure.

title: Maybe, if you’re going
audio: Silent; no music or recorded voiceover.
captionSidecarNote: SRT covers the full duration with draft voiceover text; the video itself is silent.
caption: Interested, Down if friends go, or Going? Sometimes the honest answer changes as a plan gets closer. We’re building Yard to give each answer a clear place.
cta: Which one sounds most like your usual first answer?

scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: There’s “save it for later.”
There’s “I’m in if my friends are.”
And there’s “see you there.”

scenes.onScreen: Plans that feel like you. · yard.
scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: We’re building Yard so each kind of yes has a place.

title: Three small ways to feel less new in a new city
audio: Silent; no music or recorded voiceover.
captionSidecarNote: SRT covers the full duration with draft voiceover text; the video itself is silent.
caption: A new city can feel like a lot to figure out all at once. Try making it smaller: one familiar place, one hello, one easy invite around something you already enjoy. No rush to have it all figured out.
cta: What small repeat helped you feel at home somewhere?

scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: Pick one place you’d happily go back to.
Learn one name. No need to collect a whole new friend group in a week.
Make one easy invitation around something you already like.
Belonging can begin with small repeats.

title: A little privacy, built in
audio: Silent; no music or recorded voiceover.
captionSidecarNote: SRT covers the full duration with draft voiceover text; the video itself is silent.
caption: Saving an event and committing to go are different choices. In Yard, Interested is private; Going is visible to friends and fellow attendees. We’re building that distinction into the product.
cta: What helps a social app feel comfortable to use?

scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: Saving an idea doesn’t have to be an announcement.
In Yard, Interested is private.

scenes.onScreen: Going · visible to friends and attendees
scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: Going is the choice you share with friends and fellow attendees.
Clear choices make better plans.

title: The follow-up text doesn’t need to be clever
audio: Silent; no music or recorded voiceover.
captionSidecarNote: SRT covers the full duration with draft voiceover text; the video itself is silent.
caption: A kind follow-up can be one sentence: “I liked talking about [thing]. Want to [easy activity] next week?” Specific, warm, and no pressure to answer on the spot.
cta: Save this little text template for later.

scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: Had a nice conversation and want to see them again?

scenes.onScreen: “I liked hearing about your pottery class…”
scenes.draftVoiceoverCaption: Mention the thing you talked about.
Offer one easy plan for another time.
Send the kind note. Let them answer in their own time.
